correctness.rationale: The exact compound-Poisson log PGF equals xi Σ(z_t-1)+mu(E_Q∏(1+Q(z_t-1))-1). Its distinct-visit derivatives are c1=xi+mu α/(α+β) and cr=mu(α)_r/(α+β)_r (r>=2); the entire count law is determined by these square-free coefficients. For T=4, c3/c2 and c4/c3 uniquely recover α+β, α, β, then mu and xi. For T<=3, continuity of the explicit one-parameter curve in S preserves all available cumulants and the full count law at every interior xi>0. Independently checked exact rational inversion on three profiles, common c1,c2,c3=(6,2,8/7) for two distinct sets, and fourth difference 1/147. With xi known zero, c2/c1 and c3/c2 give the analogous sharp three-visit inversion. The proof handles positive shape parameters and boundary xi=0 as stated.

value.rationale: Sharp structural identifiability with false-positive contamination is central to ecological count modeling: the result determines a minimal survey-design dimension and supplies a pair of genuinely observationally identical three-visit count laws and a complete admissible cross-cumulant region. These are useful independently of finite-sample estimation.

final_claim: Sharp 4-visit structural identifiability threshold for beta-heterogeneous Poisson abundance with unknown independent Poisson false detections
limitations: Requires closed Poisson abundance, independent persistent individual beta marks, conditional independent Bernoulli detection and independent identically distributed Poisson background across visits.
Does not cover nonparametric mark distributions, correlated backgrounds, visit-specific intensities or empirical finite-sample identifiability.
